issues.title: feat(update): launch update check + anonymous install ping, one request two jobs (#799) + patch-cadence notice (#939)
issues.body:
## What (issues #799 + #939 + the 2026-07-26 privacy ruling -- for Tuesday 07-28 build-day review)

One launch call, two jobs, per the #799 spec -- **L2 of the update ladder** (in-game update NOTICE, not a self-patcher) -- PLUS the ruled **two-tier privacy/consent model** (identity opt-in at the leaderboard; anonymous ping decoupled).

### 1. Update check
- New `UpdateCheck` autoload GETs **`https://pdoom1.com/data/version.json`** on launch: deferred, once per session, **3s hard timeout**, never blocks boot or gameplay.
- Numeric semver compare vs `GameConfig.CURRENT_VERSION` (the `"0.9.0" > "0.11.0"` string trap is unit-tested), v-prefix tolerated.
- If newer: quiet welcome-screen notice `v0.13.2 available >> [U]pdate page  [x]`. Click or **U** opens `github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/releases/latest` via `OS.shell_open`. **Never auto-downloads.** `[x]` persists dismissal per-version (no re-nag; an even-newer release notices again).
- Any failure (offline/timeout/malformed/500) = silent no-op; one `push_warning` max per session. Identical behaviour offline.

### 2. Anonymous ping (TIER 2)
- Fire-and-forget POST to **`https://analytics.pdoom1.com/api/event`** (Plausible, per #799; 202 = accepted-not-stored, never retried).
- Payload whitelist by construction: `install_id` (random UUIDv4 persisted to `user://install_id.txt`, **never machine-derived**, regenerates on reinstall by design), `version`, `os`, `first_launch`. A **privacy regression test** pins the exact key sets.
- `User-Agent: pdoom1/<version> (<OS>)` on both requests (Plausible drops UA-less; doubles as a #940 server-log signal).
- **Default ON** with an honestly-labelled Settings toggle: "Anonymous launch ping (counts installs; no personal data)".
- Headless runs (CI/GUT/--import) never do real HTTP.

### 3. Identity consent at the leaderboard (TIER 1 -- privacy ruling 2026-07-26)
- **Explicit first-time opt-in:** the first time a run reaches score submission, a one-time game-over `ConfirmationDialog` states exactly what is shared (player name, lab name, score) -- `[OK] Submit my runs` / `Keep local only`. Either answer is **persisted immediately** and never re-asked.
- **One gracious reminder, ever:** an anonymous player (empty name/lab) reaching submission un-opted-in gets a single friendly non-blocking label pointing at Settings (persisted `reminder_shown`); later playthroughs stay silent. No hounding.
- **Settings, changeable any time:** the toggle is re-labelled "Submit scores to global leaderboard (shares player + lab name)"; flipping it counts as the explicit choice. It displays the EFFECTIVE state (OFF until a real choice), so legacy default-ON configs render honestly.
- **Local play untouched:** local scores always save + display regardless of consent (asserted end-to-end); viewing the global board stays un-gated.
- Gate: `LeaderboardSync.should_submit()` = enabled + configured + `consent_asked` + opted-in. Flow routing via the pure `consent_flow_state()` (submit / ask / remind / silent), unit-tested as a matrix.
- **Migration:** pre-ruling configs persisted `submit_scores_global=true` without any explicit click -> those players get the one-time prompt at their next game over.

### 4. PING DECOUPLING -- interpretation, APPROVED by Pip
Coordinator interpretation, **approved by Pip** ("approve your subtle correction to privacy processing... good pickup"): the anonymous ping carries **no identity**, so the leaderboard gate -- which now means IDENTITY consent specifically -- no longer gates it. The ping honours exactly its own default-ON toggle. (Earlier revisions of this branch AND-gated the two; the decoupling is deliberate, prominent, and a one-line revert in `UpdateCheck.should_send_ping` if Pip flips on Tuesday.)

### 5. Docs -- anti-policy-rot (per Pip's instruction with the approval)
- **`docs/PRIVACY_POSTURE.md` (NEW, canonical SSOT):** the two-tier model stated plainly with rationale (identity consent and anonymous counting are different consent classes), ruling date, decoupling statement, cross-links to `user_privacy.json`, the settings screen, #799/#940.
- **`user_privacy.json`** rewritten from the stray Python-era artifact (single-quoted pseudo-JSON; nothing live reads it -- the Python tests use tempdirs) into a valid-JSON v2 posture record matching the ruled model; every legacy key preserved verbatim under `legacy_python_era` for provenance. No stale opt-in-flavour text contradicts shipped behaviour.
- **`docs/PRIVACY.md`** gets a pointer: posture file wins on conflict.
- `docs/game-design/DISTRIBUTION_AND_PATCHING.md` L2 entry marked SHIPPED.

### 6. Patch-cadence notice (#939, same screen)
`[!] Patching frequently right now -- updates land often` above the version string; auto-sunsets via `UpdateCheck.PATCH_CADENCE_SUNSET = "2026-08-04"` (dated constant -- removal cannot be forgotten).

### Tests
- `test_update_check.gd` (29): semver traps, ladder-epoch rejection, feed fail-closed, notice gating + dismissal, stubbed-transport handler paths, UUIDv4 shape, sunset gate, **ping payload whitelist**, **ping fires regardless of leaderboard choice**.
- `test_leaderboard_consent.gd` (NEW): full consent matrix (first-time opt-in required before any named submission; empty-name reminder exactly once ever; remembered decline silent forever), declined players still fetch/view, settings round-trip through real save/load for all five consent+privacy keys.
- `test_leaderboard_sync.gd`: consent-aware gating incl. unasked-blocks-submit-but-not-fetch.
- Game-over isolation suites: run as consented player + new end-to-end **declined-consent-keeps-score-local** case (nothing queued for remote).
- Fast gate: **788 tests, 0 failures, 84/84 files collected.** No real HTTP anywhere in tests.
- Existing local Leaderboard dedupe issue #700 untouched (out of scope).

### Follow-ups (out of scope)
- #940 consumes the ping server-side; website repo's `alpha-watch.py` starts reporting once shipped.
- Per #799: Pip must add the Plausible custom-property allow-list + Download goal on the website side (not retroactive).

Closes #799. Closes #939. Refs #940. (Squash-merge does not fire closes-keywords here -- verify/close manually after merge.)

For Tuesday 2026-07-28 build-day review.

issues.title: art: prop native-grain vanguard -- decision sheet for the ~500-gen re-base (#900, #925)
issues.body:
## What

Vanguard generation lane answering: **should office props be re-based at native pixel grain** (small canvases whose pixels land at 1 art px = 2 screen px, matching the 32px-art floor) instead of the current larger-canvas art?

Refs #900, #925. Pip decides from the sheet before the ~500-gen prop re-base fires.

## Contents

- `art_source/pixellab_2026-07-26_prop_grain_vanguard/` -- 32 PNGs + MANIFEST.md + object_ids.json:
  - `native/` (21): true-proportion candidates for water_cooler, filing_cabinet, server_cluster, **desk + door (the drawn-circle gap)**, scummy/decent tiers where the ladder has them, 40x48..112x80 canvases.
  - `manifest_scale/` (6): controls at the CURRENT oversized canvases -- isolates grain from scale.
  - `dial/` (5): medium detail/shading variants.
- `tools/art_review/gen_prop_grain_sheet.py` -- builds `art_generated/prop_grain_vanguard_sheet.html` (review_style module, verdict chips, self-contained data URIs). Already copied to the main checkout's `art_generated/` for Pip; regenerate any time.

## Sheet: what it shows

Each prop on a real concrete-floor strip (1:1 screen px) with the in-game 2-tile worker silhouette:
- (a) CURRENT art at manifest scale -- the trio renders **3.25-3.5 tiles tall vs a 2-tile human** (all manifest heights are `review: true`);
- (a2) CURRENT art naively shrunk to realistic proportion -- the zero-cost alternative: **sub-pixel smooth mush**;
- (b) NATIVE-GRAIN candidate at the world 2x -- right-sized AND on the floor's pixel grid;
- verdict-taggable candidate grids (promote = re-base this way).

## Measurements

- Balance 5826 -> 5793: **33 gens / 32 objects (~1.03/object)** -- first Tier 3 figures; Tier 3 pool reads 7419/month. 5 submissions rate-limited at ~14 in flight (unbilled), refired fine.
- Clean-alpha scan: all 32 PNGs, 0 halo / 0 speckle px.

## Lane eyeball read

Native grain wins -- but the sheet shows the current art's real defect is **proportion** (props towering over workers), and fixing proportion by downscaling makes mush; native re-gen fixes both at once. Manifest-scale control re-gens stay glossy/fine-grained, evidence the canvas size (not a re-roll) is the lever. Weak rolls flagged in MANIFEST (desk_scummy r1, water_cooler_scummy r1).

No `godot/` changes.

Gentle-now action: one daily_metrics.json schema + a scheduled snapshot appender (website repo or pdoom-data owns it -- cross-repo call via Pip per protocol); pdoom1 side = #799 ping + the people-hours formula documented. issues.body:
# Spec: one launch call that does two jobs

**For: `PipFoweraker/pdoom1`, in tonight's build if at all possible.**
Written 2026-07-22. Self-contained — hand this straight to the build.

## Why this is the one thing worth stopping for

Two problems, one HTTP call:

1. **You cannot count players.** The only game-to-server signal today is a score
   submission, which needs the player to finish a run AND not have opted out.
   `entry_uuid` is per-entry, so it cannot even dedupe people. v0.11.0 shows 135
   asset downloads on GitHub and there is no way to tell how many were humans
   rather than scanners — an install ID is the only thing that answers that.

2. **You cannot tell an existing player that a patch exists.** The game has
   `has_unseen_patch_notes()` in `godot/autoload/game_config.gd:368`, but it
   compares `last_seen_version != CURRENT_VERSION` — **both local**. That shows
   patch notes *after* someone updates; it cannot tell someone on v0.11.0 that
   v0.12.0 shipped. There is no remote version check anywhere in the Godot
   project.

Neither can be retrofitted onto builds already in players' hands. Every cohort
that downloads without this stays uncountable and unreachable **forever**. That
is the whole argument for the 36-hour window.

---

## The call

One request on launch. Fire-and-forget, async, never blocking startup.

### Request

```
POST https://analytics.pdoom1.com/api/event
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: <must be set to a real UA string; Plausible drops requests without one>

{
  "name": "Game Launch",
  "domain": "pdoom1.com",
  "url": "app://pdoom1/launch",
  "props": {
    "install_id":   "<uuid-v4>",
    "version":      "0.12.0",
    "os":           "Windows",
    "first_launch": true
  }
}
```

Verified live: the endpoint is up, `/api/health` reports Postgres and ClickHouse
both `ok`, and a test event returned `202`. **No new server code is needed.**

Plausible returns `202` for essentially anything, so a `202` means "accepted",
not "stored" — do not treat it as confirmation. Fire and forget; never retry in a
loop, never block on it.

### `install_id` rules

- UUIDv4, generated **once**, persisted to `user://`.
- **Never** derived from hardware, MAC, disk serial, username or anything else
  about the machine. A random UUID regenerated on reinstall is exactly right —
  it counts installs, which is what we want, and it is not a device fingerprint.
- Regenerating on reinstall is fine and expected. Do not try to make it survive.

### Consent

Gate it behind the existing privacy opt-out (the same one
`godot/autoload/leaderboard_sync.gd:85-91` already honours for score
submission). If the player has opted out, **do not send at all** — not an
anonymised version, nothing.

Reuse the async + durable-outbox pattern already proven in `leaderboard_sync.gd`.
Do not invent a second networking path.

---

## The update check (same launch, second job)

Read the current version from the website, which already publishes it:

```
GET https://pdoom1.com/data/version.json
```

```json
{ "latest_release": { "version": "v0.12.0", "published_at": "..." } }
```

That file is live now, auto-updated by a workflow, and served as static JSON off
DreamHost — no API, no auth, no rate limit worth worrying about.

Compare `latest_release.version` against the local `CURRENT_VERSION`. If the
remote is newer, show a non-blocking notice on the welcome screen:

> **v0.12.0 is available** — you're on v0.11.0. [Get it]

pointing at `https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/releases/latest`.

### Rules that matter

- **Never block startup or gameplay on this.** If the request fails, times out,
  or the JSON is malformed, show nothing and carry on silently. An update check
  that can break launch is worse than no update check.
- **Compare semver numerically, not as strings.** `"0.9.0" > "0.11.0"` is true
  for string comparison and would tell every v0.11.0 player they are ahead.
  Parse to integer triples.
- Tolerate the `v` prefix being present or absent on either side.
- Do not auto-download or auto-update. Show a notice and a link; the player
  decides.
- Make it dismissible, and don't re-nag every launch for the same version.

Note this is a plain static-file read with no identifiers attached — it carries
no privacy cost and does not need to sit behind the analytics opt-out. Keep the
two concerns separate in the code even though they happen at the same moment.

---

## Order of value if time is short

1. **`install_id` + launch ping** — un-retrofittable, and the only way to know
   whether those 135 downloads were people.
2. **Update check** — un-retrofittable *for this cohort*: players who install
   v0.12.0 without it can't be told about v0.13.0 either. Every release you ship
   without it extends the problem.
3. Everything else in `GAME_REPO_ASKS_ALPHA.md` (the bug-report panel's false
   "we'll create a GitHub issue soon" message, the `F8`-vs-`N` mismatch, the
   `/contributors` 404) can wait for the fast-follow.

If only one lands tonight, make it #1.

---

## What the website side already does, so you don't duplicate it

- Publishes `/data/version.json` with `latest_release.version`. Live.
- Accepts the launch ping at `analytics.pdoom1.com/api/event`. Live, returns 202.
- Counts arrivals and download clicks via Plausible. **Pip must add a `Download`
  Goal and allow the custom properties in Plausible settings before links go out
  — property allow-listing is not retroactive.**
- `scripts/alpha-watch.py` reads both streams and will start reporting install
  counts as soon as the ping exists.

Nothing on the website blocks any of this.

---

*Filed from `pdoom1-website`. Full spec also at `docs/GAME_SPEC_launch_ping_and_update_check.md` in that repo. Website side is ready and blocks none of this.*

issues.title: ui: attention items force left-hand action menu to compact with inconsistent item sizes

labels.name: patch:ui
labels.description: Mid-week UI hotpatch -- non-forking, ships any time, does not disturb the live league

issues.body:
FIRST EXTERNAL PLAYER FEEDBACK -- reported by Barry (friend tester), 2026-07-26, on the v0.13.1 Windows release, ~turn 87 of a real run.

Barry: 'if you add attention items they force the left hand menu to compact -- some items its like 12 some 14 some more.'

Read: as Attention queue items accumulate (screenshot shows Attention: 20, 8 free / 12 queued), the left-hand action menu compacts and individual items render at inconsistent sizes (~12px vs ~14px vs more). Likely layout container pressure from the top-bar attention counter propagating into the action list (layout_controller.gd / main_ui.gd territory).

Screenshot also confirms in the wild: the DEV BUILD badge shows on the release build -- that is the known build_stamp.txt-not-in-pck bug, already fixed for the NEXT tag by #904/#919; not Barry's issue.

Repro: long run, accumulate attention/queued items past ~12-20, observe left menu.

issues.title: tools(art): cycle-closeout script -- move assets to their right home when a generation cycle finishes
issues.body:
Pip note-in-passing 2026-07-26, while reviewing the cat sweep: 'a little cleanup script at the end of the art generation cycles that moves things to the right spot in the repo and/or storage once we're done actively working on them.'

Design sketch (reuses existing machinery + conventions):
- INPUT: the verdict state (pixellab_verdicts.json / hero_verdicts.json) + analyzer lists for a named batch dir (e.g. art_source/pixellab_2026-07-26_cat_sweep/).
- ACTIONS per policy: promoted assets confirmed tracked (art_generated keep-only-promoted force-add convention; art_source batches already all-tracked per the commit-all-PNGs rule); wired assets copied into godot/assets/** with mapping entries; >1MB masters verified OUT of git and present in G:/tmp/pdoom1-art-masters/ (tools/archive_masters.py exists, unrun); fully-triaged batch dirs get a CLOSEOUT stamp in their MANIFEST.md (date, verdict counts, disposition) so 'done actively working' is a legible state; derived HTML sheets confirmed gitignored.
- SAFETY: dry-run default (report the move plan), --apply to execute; never deletes rejected art (negative evidence is kept by standing rule); refuses if the batch has untriaged items unless --partial.
- Cross-links: repo-slim findings (art_source 124MB tracked), tools/slim_repo.py, DOC_LIFECYCLE.md pattern, #925 pre-build epic.
Natural first customers: the four 2026-07-26 batch dirs once Pip's cat-sweep triage lands.

issues.title: tools(art-review): verdict provenance -- timestamped, append-only progression capture
issues.body:
Pip 2026-07-26 (after exporting a dated verdict file to differentiate his session): 'we might want to think about a subtle upgrade to capture progressions of values in a stately and timestamped fashion.'

Design sketch: keep the current canonical snapshot (pixellab_verdicts.json / hero_verdicts.json -- what the analyzer reads) but add an append-only event log per library (e.g. art_source/verdict_log.jsonl): one line per verdict change {ts, session_id, path, tags_before, tags_after, source: sheet|in-engine|agent}. The sheet export gains timestamps + session id; the fold step appends the delta to the log; snapshots stay derived+small. This gives: value progressions over time (did Pip warm to a style?), session provenance for the cost model's triage-rate estimates (currently +/-2x for lack of timestamps -- see SEED_ART_COST_MODEL LIMITS), and safe replay of any snapshot state. The in-engine #848 cycler writes the same event shape.

Anti-goal: do NOT make the canonical snapshot a log (analyzer stays simple; the log is additive).

issues.title: office: W3 pre-build -- decision-agnostic engineering so W3 rulings flow into builds without decision fatigue
issues.body:
Pip's framing 2026-07-26: 'what do we want to pre-build with flexibility so the decisions from W3 flow to build patterns with less decision fatigue about engineering we can preload now.' Candidate pre-builds -- each is decision-AGNOSTIC (no W3 ruling is burned by building it):

1. **Tile-grid addressing INTERFACE** behind the existing fraction-addressed room: a room->grid mapping API with fraction fallback, so W3's tile-grid ruling becomes a switch-flip migration, not a rewrite. (The single biggest fatigue-saver; gates tier-2 pathing.)
2. **Prop manifest placement metadata** (schema v1.2): wall-mounted vs floor flag, against-wall, approach-points (fixes 'stands in front of the water cooler' generically -- stand-slots per prop), zone tags (kitchen/desk/door). Data only.
3. **Room layout format**: named-slot JSON room templates (door position, wall segments, window slots, table zones) + loader, replacing hardcoded bounds fractions. W3 decides layout CONTENT; the format + loader pre-exist.
4. **Furniture as assets**: tables/desks render from manifest props instead of drawn circles. Pure uplift, no decision dependency.
5. **Wall/floor tileset variation**: per-room tileset selection from data (tier ladder scummy/decent/premium already exists); supports Pip's 'multiple tilesets for wall spaces'.
6. **Office-fullness primitive**: occupancy metric (footprint cells used / walkable cells) exposed on the floor -- the interior-decorating math W3 will want as an input.
7. **#848 A/B cycler** (already planned) -- the decision-accelerator itself.

Sequencing suggestion: 2+4+6 are small and ride office passes; 1+3 are a focused pre-W3 lane; 5 follows the wall-tileset generation.
